questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word segment in the given sentence. If the sentence is grammatically correct, select ‘No correction’.

Neha is writing a letter when I called her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The highlighted phrase "**is writing**" is incorrect in the context of the sentence.
 
• The sentence indicates a past event, so the verb tense must align with the past tense.
 
• The correct tense is "**was writing**," which shows that Neha was in the middle of writing the letter when the call occurred.
 
• Thus, the correct substitution for the highlighted phrase is **"was writing" (Option 3).**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Neha was writing a letter when I called her."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "is being written" **– This is grammatically incorrect because it suggests passive voice, which does not fit the context.
 
• **Option 2: "writes"** – This is incorrect because it refers to a habitual action, whereas the sentence describes a specific past event.
 
• **Option 4: "No correction"** – This is incorrect because the original sentence contains a tense error.
 
• **Option 3: "was writing"** – This is the correct option as it uses the past continuous tense to describe the action happening at the time of the call.
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

“Camila helps her mother in cooking dinner, __isn’t she__?” asked Veronica.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question tag must agree with the main verb and subject of the sentence.
 
• Here, the main verb is "**helps**," which is in the present tense, and the subject is "**Camila**," a singular noun.
 
• The correct question tag for a positive statement with a singular subject in the present tense is "**doesn't she**."
 
• Thus, "**doesn't she**" is the appropriate replacement for the underlined segment.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Camila helps her mother in cooking dinner, doesn't she?" asked Veronica.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: hasn't she** – Incorrect as it refers to the present perfect tense, which doesn't match the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: don't she** – Incorrect because "don't" does not agree with a singular subject.
 
• **Option 4: wasn't she** – Incorrect as it refers to the past tense, while the sentence is in the present tense.
</ul

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**ensuring**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The sentence discusses the positive outcomes that could have resulted from enlightened policy approaches after the first NFHS was conducted.
 
• The blank requires a word that shows the result or aim of these actions, which is that no child or woman is left behind in health efforts.
 
• "**Ensuring**" is the most appropriate word, as it indicates making certain that all individuals benefit from health initiatives.
 
• Other options like "**suggesting**", "**searching**", and "**avoiding**" do not fit the context of guaranteeing positive outcomes for all.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The National Family Health Survey (NFHS) mentioned in its report how effectively India has used its newly created wealth to alter a dismal record of nutritional deprivation, ill-health and lost potential among__ its citizens, particularly women and children. Given the steady growth in real per capita GDP since the 1980s, and the progress made since Independence in overcoming severe undernourishment, enlightened policy approaches could have brought about a giant leap from 1992-93, when the first NFHS was conducted, __ensuring__ that no child or woman was left behind in the quest for health for all. Evidently, the Indian state has not viewed the situation as constituting a national crisis, even at the height of a prosperous phase of economic growth when a decade ago 39% of children under the age of five remained underweight. It comes as no surprise, therefore, that this failure to assume responsibility for child nutrition has left 34% of children in that age group underweight today. There is also a lot of evidence to show that the __poorest__ sections of India’s children have low weight even at birth due to the general __neglect__ of women’s nutrition and well-being. It is imperative that the coming data lead to the charting of a new policy course that makes __access__ to nutrition and health a right for all.*
